page.layout: Top: two circular portrait medallions with inscriptions around their rims, side by side (left: PTOLOMAEVS, right: ELEAZARVS). Below them: one column of running text, two paragraphs. Below the text: a fleuron ornament (not transcribed). No margin notes, no footnote lines.

main_text.p: PTOLOMAEVS Philadelphus, superioris Ptolomæi filius iunior, successit patri in regno Ægypti, anno mundi 3680. ante Christum natum 282. hic Stratonis discipulus doctissimus fuit:Bibliothecam insignem parauit Alexandriæ. Iudæos qui in Ægypto erant, liberos esse permisit, & vasa Eleazaro summo sacerdoti Ierosolymorum, votiua transmittens, diuinas scripturas in Græcam linguam per septuaginta interpretes verti curauit. Huius frater maior natu, qui Seleucum vita regnoque Macedoniæ priuauerat, amicitiam, pacemque ac concordiam per epistolas deprecatur, professus deponere se offensam erepti paterni regni, neque amplius à fratre quæsiturum quod honestius à paterno hoste percepisset. Eutr.lib.2. Iusti.lib.17.D.Epipha.in lib.de ponde. & mensuris.Iose. lib.Antiqui.12.cap.2. Titus Liu.Deca.5.lib.4.&5.

ELEAZARVS, patri Oniæ, cognominato iusto, successit in pontificatu Iudæorum, anno mundi 3691. ante Christum natum 271. Ad hunc scripsit Ptolemæus Philadelphus, hic quoque ad illum: extant utriusque epistolæ apud Iosephum lib.Antiquit.12.cap.2. Misit hic ad Ptolemæum libros Mosaicæ legis, atque ex unaquaque tribu senos viros interpretes, Hebraicè Græcéque peritissimos. Consulito D.Augustin.[?]lib.de ciuit.Dei 18.cap.42.

page.notes: Medallion inscriptions: the first letter of the right-hand medallion (read as E) is doubtful and the inscription is partly obscured by the portrait; marked [?]. Printed numbers copied as they stand (3680, 282, 3691, 271). The name after "D." in the second paragraph is hard to read on the scan (printed long s/ligature); read as Augustin with [?]. Printed spacing and the colon in "fuit:Bibliothecam" kept as printed. Page number 139 printed at the top right, running head PARS PRIMA. at the top centre.
